reasoning:
I need to replace the nearest-neighbour arc procedure with a slot-and-swap rule in both the annotator prompt and the memory policy prompt, keeping the subgoal unchanged since the report gives no indication otherwise. The slot-and-swap framing comes from the minibatch's claim, so I'll accept it but phrase it generally—something like "when the two return, each sits in the other's slot"—to also cover edge cases where the swap behaves differently.

I'll commit to the swap rule since the report consistently states swapping occurs in this task; the policy just can't distinguish the containers after circling, so the swap assumption resolves that ambiguity. Now I'm drafting the actual edits: swapping out the old "target_containers" annotation text about tracking containers frame-to-frame for the new slot-and-swap description, and replacing the Procedure steps in the policy prompt with the equivalent logic, then outputting it all as JSON.

edits.modify_from: Procedure: (1) from the first demonstration frames note the position of each named cube; (2) at the first frame where containers are listed instead of cubes, the named cube's container is the one nearest that cube's position; (3) follow that container through the remaining demonstration frames: at each frame it is the listed container nearest to its position in the previous frame, and when two moving containers are nearly equally near, keep the one that continues the same arc (the container that moved toward larger y keeps the larger y, the one that moved toward smaller y keeps the smaller y); containers that never move keep their position; (4) its position in the last demonstration frame is the entry. e.g. [[81, 90], [87, 134]]
edits.modify_to: Procedure: (1) from the first demonstration frames note each named cube's position; (2) at the first frame listing containers, the named cube's container is the one nearest that cube; the positions listed in that frame are the slots; label the named container by its slot; (3) go through the remaining frames; whenever a frame lists two containers at positions that are not slots (off by well over 10 pixels), a shuffle is under way between the two containers whose slots are now empty; it lasts until a frame again shows all containers at slots; at that frame those two containers have SWAPPED slots, so if the named container was one of the two, its slot is now the other container's old slot; a second shuffle of the same pair swaps them back; shuffles of other pairs do not change its slot; (4) never assume a container returns to its own starting slot, and never take the container resting nearest the cube's original position in the last frame; the entry is the named container's slot after every swap, written with that slot's coordinates as listed in the last demonstration frame. Worked example: cube at [70, 119]; containers first rest at [66, 120], [84, 109], [93, 163], [119, 145]; the cube's container is [66, 120]; later frames show [66, 120] and [84, 109] both off their slots for three frames, then all back; those two swapped, so the cube's container is now the one at [84, 110] in the last frame; entry [84, 110]. e.g. [[84, 110], [93, 163]]
